supersedes.why: Both encode the D-011 reasoning that D-013 OVERTURNED. They assert the disabled witness is unobtainable because 'Acceptance forbids calling, sending, launching', and cite phone-app/packages/ui/src/index.tsx. D-013 established that the no-launch/no-call clause is a CONSTRAINT ON THE METHOD, not proof of unreachability: the matrix asks for a source decision plus a visible explanation, which is exactly what this artifact supplies. additional-states.json .phone.disabled is [] and phone-disabled.png (sha256 8fac1449...) shows the ENABLED 'Book a call / Create invite' form, so neither is r-2 evidence for the disabled case.

correction.what: An earlier revision of this file justified the claim above by asserting that 'the 4-file drift set contains no UI source'. That rationale was WRONG and is withdrawn. The blob-identity measurement it was attached to was and remains correct; only the reasoning offered for it was false.
correction.why: It conflated two different baselines. D-012's 4-file drift set is measured against the RUNNING RELEASE BUILD EPOCH (05:11:25Z), not against the graded commit. The graded-commit delta is larger: git diff --stat 88afe6a7 6090a4d6 = 7 files, and it DOES include UI source — packages/ui/src/shell.tsx and packages/ui/src/shell-model.ts (the preference-race fix), plus tests/preference-refresh.test.ts.
correction.why_it_does_not_change_the_claim: Release-independence here rests on a per-file blob comparison of voice-session.tsx, not on a whole-tree assertion. Other UI files changing is irrelevant to whether THIS file did, and it did not.
correction.note_for_the_grader: The preference fix was authored at 05:07Z, entered the running release built at 05:11:25Z, and was only COMMITTED at 05:44Z by git-sync. So release Jk8vf6ox...051125119 contains UI source that its nominal graded HEAD 88afe6a7 does not. Judge that release by its sourceRootDigest and source manifest, not by the graded commit id.

designIntentInSource.verbatim: Offered-but-disabled with an explanatory title, the same choice workspaces.tsx argues for: removing the control entirely reads as "this surface has no push-to-talk", where a quiet disabled one with its precondition teaches what has to be true. What it must NOT do is stay live and swallow the press.
designIntentInSource.why_it_matters: r-2 asks whether disabled treatments describe the real actionable state. The source states that requirement as its own design rule and implements it: one decision function drives the disabled attribute, the visible status, the tooltip and the accessible name together.

verdictForR2Phone.reasoning: The Phone/voice surface's disabled state is decided in one auditable source function whose every unavailable branch returns a distinct reason, and that reason reaches the viewer through a visible aria-live status line, a tooltip and the control's accessible name, while the control is genuinely disabled by the same verdict. Four of six branches also name the remedy. This satisfies stateCases[1] by its own prescribed method.
verdictForR2Phone.scope: This artifact proves the PHONE half of the 'workspaces-and-phone' surface group. The WORKSPACES half was already accepted by the prior grader ('disabled Workspace actions with state-specific explanations'), and workspace-disabled-status.png is the standing capture for it.
